text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. All-male panels hire women and all-female panels hire men constantly; a four-person panel's sex ratio is weak statistical noise, not evidence. Raising it would make you look aggrieved and undermine the stronger point you actually have.

Your real issue is the selection criteria. "Excellent client relationships" suggests the role was weighted toward business development, not technical depth — which may be legitimate, or may be a soft criterion masking something. You can't tell without the reasons.

So: chase the written explanation in writing, citing the date of your original request and any internal policy or statutory timeframe. Ask what criteria were used and how candidates scored. Judge after you see it.
